## Triage — graded **`bug`**, routed **`domain:ui`**, `pm:queue`. This outranks the card that produced it.

By the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Graded immediately rather than at the next round boundary, because it is the only user-visible defect to come out of this lane tonight.

### Why `bug` and not `finding`

Everything else in the #4905 / #3512 / #3865 family is about **gate coverage** — a pin that could not reach a call site. This is not that. On a provider-less host, 65 inline defaults across 24 files render `{{name}}` to the user **as literal braces**. That is a rendering defect on `main` today, reachable by a real user, with no gate anywhere covering it: it is a **different code path** from #3865 and #3512, which is precisely why the existing pins are green over it.

### Why `domain:ui` and not this lane

⛔ Out of `domain:devx`. The remedy is per-call-site work in `packages/app-shell` and friends — deciding, site by site, whether the fix is to bind a translation hook whose fallback interpolates, or to keep the pre-interpolated template literal and stop treating it as residue. That is renderer/authoring-surface judgement, not tooling. This seat would be picking UI conventions it does not own.

### The mechanism, so the receiving lane does not re-derive it

`react-i18next`'s not-ready `t` (`notReadyT`) returns `options.defaultValue` **verbatim, without interpolating**. So at a site bound to a bare `useObjectTranslation()`, a default carrying `{{holes}}` reaches the DOM with the braces intact. The contrast that makes it tractable is already measured on #4905: `useDetailTranslation` — a `createSafeTranslation` factory whose `fallbackT` **does** interpolate — is safe, and `DetailSection.tsx:493` is the worked example of a hole that is fine for that reason.

⭐ **The corollary is the part that must not be lost, because it inverts an assumption three of us held.** For these sites the pre-interpolated template literal is the *correct* spelling, not residue. #4905's dispatch order (mine), its triage, and the card body all assumed the opposite and specified a rewrite that would have **introduced** this defect at 29 more sites. The dev applied it, watched a test go red, bisected to one line, read the library source, and reverted. ⛔ So any remedy here that mechanically rewrites template literals into `{{hole}}` form is walking into the same wall — the rewrite is only safe where the bound `t` interpolates on the fallback path, and that has to be established per hook, not per file.

### What a resolution should produce

- The per-hook fact first: which translation bindings interpolate on the provider-less path and which do not. Everything else follows from that table, and it does not exist anywhere yet.
- Then the 24 files judged against it — some will need a different hook, some are already correct and should be recorded as correct so the next sweep does not "fix" them.
- ⚠️ A pin, or this recurs. But ⛔ do not specify the pin before the table exists: a gate written against the wrong model of which defaults are correct is exactly how #4905's order went wrong.

### Bound

⛔ Not blocked by anything, and ⛔ not addressed by PR #6218 — that PR's class 7 judges default *spelling* against the drift rule and does not know which hook a site binds. `pm:queue` rather than dispatched: it needs a `domain:ui` seat, and this one will not take it.

Refs: #4905 / PR #6218 (where the mechanism was measured, with the 29-site reversion and its reasoning) · #3512 · #3865 (the adjacent, different code path).

## Claimed + dispatched — `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat

PM session `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`, branch `claude/issue-6219-notready-t-interpolation`.
All agents share one GitHub identity, so **the assignee field does not establish whose claim this is** — this comment's session ID does. An earlier claim comment with a different session ID outranks this one; there is none on this card.

### 裁决 (binding — do not re-open)

**Both triage comments agree and I ratify the one-seam direction as the route to attempt FIRST: teach the provider's not-ready path to interpolate, rather than migrating 65 call sites.** That is option 3 on the card body ("teach `useObjectTranslation` to interpolate its own not-ready result").

⚠️ It is ratified as the **preferred route, not as a mandate over measurement.** The card records a real objection to it: objectui#3512 explicitly declined to fork from react-i18next's behaviour in the other direction. If you measure that the one-seam fix cannot be made without breaking a pin that #3512 or #3865 owns, **stop and report** — do not silently fall back to the 24-file migration, and do not overrule #3512 yourself. That fork is mine to rule, and I will rule it same-round.

### PM机制假设 (verify — each of these can be wrong, and one of them already burned this family once)

1. `useObjectTranslation` returns react-i18next's `t` directly from `packages/i18n/src/provider.tsx`, so a bare call site with no provider gets `notReadyT`. **Re-derive this by reading the file** — the card measured it, but on an older `main`.
2. The 24-file / 65-default census still holds on today's `main`. Re-run the sweep; report the delta rather than inheriting the number.
3. `notReadyT` returns `options.defaultValue` verbatim and does **not** interpolate. Verify against the installed `react-i18next` in `node_modules`, not against the card's quoted source.
4. `createSafeTranslation`'s `fallbackT` **does** interpolate (`value.split(\`{{${k}}}\`).join(String(v))`). This is the contrast that makes the whole card tractable — confirm it.

### ⭐ The corollary that must not be lost — it inverted an assumption three people held

Triage states this and I am restating it because it is the single most expensive fact on this card:

> For these sites the **pre-interpolated template literal is the CORRECT spelling, not residue.** objectui#4905's dispatch order, its triage, and its card body all assumed the opposite and specified a rewrite that would have **introduced** this defect at 29 more sites. The dev applied it, watched a test go red, bisected to one line, read the library source, and reverted.

⛔ **Therefore: any remedy that mechanically rewrites template literals into `{{hole}}` form is walking into the same wall.** That rewrite is only safe where the bound `t` interpolates on the provider-less path, and that must be established **per hook**, not per file.

### What the resolution must produce (triage's ordering, which I adopt)

1. **The per-hook table FIRST** — which translation bindings interpolate on the provider-less path and which do not. It does not exist anywhere yet, and everything else follows from it.
2. Then the affected files judged against that table. **Some will already be correct, and those must be recorded as correct** so the next sweep does not "fix" them into defects.
3. A pin — but ⛔ **do not specify the pin before the table exists.** A gate written against the wrong model of which defaults are correct is exactly how #4905's order went wrong.

### Serial / collision bounds — binding

- ⛔ **Do not touch `scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs`.** It is owned by objectui#4905 / PR #6218, in flight right now. Its class 7 judges default *spelling* and does not know which hook a site binds; extending it to take the binding's factory as an input is that card's to do, not yours. If your work implies that extension, **report it as a finding** and let #4905 land first.
- Four sibling agents are running this wave on `packages/plugin-view`, `packages/plugin-gantt`, `packages/plugin-form` and `packages/components/src/renderers/form/radio-group.tsx`. If your census reaches any of those paths, **report the overlap rather than editing across it**.
- If the one-seam fix holds, your diff should be `packages/i18n/src/provider.tsx` + tests + changeset, and the collision surface is empty. That is another reason to attempt it first.

### Standing verification rules (non-negotiable, and this card has a specific trap)

Predict direction before running. Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and** separately the removed text. Print the landing site. Assert anchor uniqueness bounded to the right span. Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a cwd-independent command, and confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty afterwards. Derive the gate set by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**, not top-level script names. A cached turbo green is not a measurement — use `--force`. Commit before you ablate.

⚠️ **The trap specific to this card:** a test that renders with `I18nProvider` mounted can never see this defect — i18next is ready, the pack value wins, and the inline default never renders at all. A pin that mounts the provider is a **phantom assertion**, true regardless of the fix. The pin must render provider-less, and must assert on the **rendered DOM text**, not on the return value of a `t` you called yourself.

State plainly in the PR body **which of your assertions would still pass on a revert**, and why each of those is there.

⛔ Leave the PR **draft**. Do not mark ready, do not enqueue, do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it.

### Notes for the PM that do not fit the JSON

- **The one-seam route held; no `blocked` was needed.** The #3512 stop-and-report
  condition was checked as a measurement, not assumed away: #3512's resolution
  (PR #4904) was to *gate the copy* to `{{name}}` rather than widen the fallback's
  grammar, so extending that same single grammar to one more *binding* is
  continuous with it. The only #3512-owned artefact that reacted was its
  `NEEDLE_FILES` completeness registry, which correctly noticed the interpolator
  had moved file. That is the pin doing its job, not breaking.
- **Serial bound honoured.** `scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` is untouched
  even though your update lifted the prohibition — after reading what #6218
  actually landed, the measured conclusion is that it needs **no** extension for
  this card. Its class 7 already holds every inline default to the one spelling;
  what it lacked was a world where that rule was true at every binding, and that
  is exactly what this PR supplies. Extending it to read a binding's *factory*
  would now gate a distinction that no longer exists.
- **Zero collision surface.** The diff is `packages/i18n/**` plus one changeset.
  Nothing under `plugin-view`, `plugin-gantt`, `plugin-form` or
  `components/.../radio-group.tsx` was read for edit or written.
- **PR #6255 is DRAFT.** Not marked ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge.
- **CI not waited on**, per the standing contract — report is delivered at draft-PR
  time.
